name: Directional measuring element qualifier
summary: Arrow qualifier on a measuring relay showing that it operates only for power or current in the marked direction.
description: A directional qualifier is an arrow added to a measuring relay symbol, showing that the element responds only when the measured quantity flows in the indicated direction. On single-line diagrams the arrow usually points away from or towards the busbar, which tells the reader which faults the element is meant to see.

The arrow depends on correct CT and VT polarity to mean anything in practice. The symbol does not show the characteristic angle or the polarising quantity, so the drawing direction must be confirmed against the relay settings and commissioning tests.
readingNotes: Note whether the arrow points towards or away from the busbar.
Check CT and VT polarity supports the shown direction.
drawingChecklist: Show arrow relative to the busbar
distinction: A directional qualifier restricts operation to one direction; a non-directional element operates for either direction.

facts.label: Meaning
facts.value: Operation in the arrow direction only
